fields.System.Title: EPIC RPL — Replenishment
fields.System.Description:
Goal

Pick faces are refilled from bulk storage before a picker finds them empty.

Business value

A picker who arrives at an empty pick face loses the trip, shorts the line, and creates an
exception that a supervisor has to resolve. The stock was in the building the whole time.

Replenishment is pure efficiency work: it does not change what the warehouse can do, it
changes how much walking and how many exceptions it takes to do it.

Scope

In. Min and max rules per product per pick location. Reactive triggering on stock
movement. Source location selection with FEFO. Task creation with duplicate prevention. Task
execution with scan confirmation. Demand-driven replenishment from wave demand.

Out. Deciding which products belong in pick faces at all — that is slotting, and it is a
separate discipline. Purchasing and reordering.

Done when

  • A pick face dropping below its minimum creates exactly one task, however many times the
  • trigger fires.
  • Source selection respects FEFO and prefers a location that covers the whole need.
  • No source available raises an alert on the supervisor's exception list.
  • Tasks are confirmed with source and destination scans.
  • Wave release triggers replenishment ahead of picking, not during it.

Key risks

| Risk | Why it matters | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| Task storm | Twenty tasks for one shortage; task list unusable | [doc 09 §7.1](../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Min and max set too close | Constant refilling; wasted labour | [doc 09 §7.2](../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| No source found, nobody told | Pick face silently runs dry mid-wave | [doc 09 §7.3](../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Competing with allocation for bulk stock | Either can fail unpredictably | [doc 09 §7.4](../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Replenishment completes after the wave is picked | Wasted trip; pickers already shorted | [doc 05 WF 11](../../docs/05-workflows.md) |
